apoc_text: Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.
old_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19) The wisdom-stream names the scourging-and-mockery program the ungodly devise for the righteous one: *examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* John 19:1-5 walks the same — Pilate scourges him, the soldiers crown him with thorns and smite him, and he is brought forth meek and patient under the *despitefulness and torture* the wisdom-stream had already named as the test the ungodly impose on the just.
new_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). *Then came Yahusha (Jesus) forth, wearing the crown of thorns, and the purple robe. And Pilate saith unto them, Behold the man!* (John 19:5). Here is the program the ungodly lay out: despitefulness and torture, to see what the righteous man's meekness and patience are made of. John 19 shows it carried out to the letter — Pilate scourged him, the soldiers wove him a crown of thorns and dressed him in purple and struck him, and then he was led out before the crowd. Behold the man. He came forth meek and patient under the very test Wisdom said the ungodly would devise, and the test proved what they refused to see.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* The scourging and the crown of thorns at John 19:1–5 are this test carried out, and *Behold the man* is the answer.

apoc_text: We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.
old_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16) The righteous one of the wisdom-stream is grievous to the ungodly precisely because his life is of *another fashion* and he *makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* John 18:38's Pilate finds *no fault at all* in him, yet the chief priests press for his death on exactly the ground the wisdom-stream named — that he claims the Father as his own. The fault the ungodly find is not a crime; it is the righteousness that reproves them.
new_note: *We are esteemed of him as counterfeits: he abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:16). *Pilate saith unto him, What is truth? And when he had said this, he went out again unto the Yahudim (Jews), and saith unto them, I find in him no fault at all.* (John 18:38). Pilate looked for a crime and found none. The men pressing for his death had no crime to show either, only what Wisdom had already named: a man whose life rebuked theirs and who made his boast that Yahuah (God) was his father. That was the whole charge — he claimed the Father as his own, and his righteousness made their religion look like counterfeit. The fault the ungodly find in the just is never a crime; it is the reproof they feel just by standing near him.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:16 — *he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed, and makes his boast that Yahuah (God) is his father.* Pilate found no fault at all (John 18:38); the only charge was the one Wisdom named.

apoc_text: He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).
old_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13) The charge the Yahudim (Jews) bring at John 19:7 — *we have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Elohim (God)* — is the exact accusation the wisdom-stream put in the mouth of the ungodly against the righteous one: that *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The self-designation that the ungodly treat as the capital offence in Wisdom 2 is the self-designation the chief priests treat as the capital offence at the trial.
new_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13). *The Yahudim (Jews) answered him, We have a law, and by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Elohim (God).* (John 19:7). The charge the accusers bring to Pilate, *by our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of Elohim (God)*, is word for word the complaint Wisdom of Solomon put in the mouth of the ungodly against the righteous one: he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God). What the plotters of Wisdom 2 treat as the offence worth killing for is what the chief priests treat as the capital offence at the trial. They did not invent the charge; they inherited it from men who had been laying in wait for the righteous since before there was a Pilate to bring it to. And the law they appealed to was the law his life had been reproving them with.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The capital charge of John 19:7, he made himself the Son of Elohim (God), is the complaint Wisdom 2:13 gives the ungodly.

apoc_text: Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12) The Hebrew library's wisdom-stream names the architecture the arrest at John 18:3 walks: the band of men and officers from the chief priests *lie in wait for the righteous* one because he is *clean contrary* to their doings and *upbraideth* them with their offending the law. The plot against the righteous one is not a New Testament novelty; the wisdom-stream had already named the lying-in-wait of the ungodly against the just man who reproves them.
new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *Judas then, having received a band of men and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.* (John 18:3). The arrest at night is the lying in wait. Judas comes with a band of men and officers sent by the chief priests and Pharisees, with lanterns and torches and weapons, for one unarmed man in a garden. Wisdom of Solomon had already named the motive: the righteous one is clean contrary to their doings and upbraids them with their offending the law. The plot against the righteous one is not a New Testament novelty; the ungodly had been lying in wait for the just man who reproves them for as long as there have been just men, and the torches in Gethsemane are that old resolve carried out.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous.* The band with lanterns and torches at John 18:3 is the lying in wait of the ungodly for the righteous one who reproves them.

apoc_text: And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.
old_note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* (Tobit 14:6). The Gentiles who *have been made partakers of their spiritual things* and owe a debt *to minister unto them in carnal things* (Romans 15:27) are the nations Tobit saw turning: *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah truly, and shall bury their idols.* The collection Paul carries to the poor saints at Jerusalem is the turning made tangible — those gathered from the nations rendering their substance back to the covenant people from whom the spiritual riches came, the idols buried and the debt of love paid.
new_note: *And all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* (Tobit 14:6). *It hath pleased them verily; and their debtors they are. For if the Gentiles have been made partakers of their spiritual things, their duty is also to minister unto them in carnal things.* (Romans 15:27). Paul is carrying a collection from the assemblies among the Gentiles to the poor saints at Jerusalem, and he calls it a debt: they received spiritual things from Jerusalem, so they owe carnal things back. The Gentiles Paul writes to are, for the most part, the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) living as Gentiles among the nations, the people Tobit said would be gathered home. Tobit saw the turning that would follow, nations turning to fear Yahuah (God) truly and burying their idols, and the next line says his people would confess him and be exalted. The collection is that turning made tangible in one generation: those who had lived among the idols sending back to the covenant people what they owed, the idols left behind and the debt of love paid.
member_note: Tobit 14:6 — *all nations shall turn, and fear Yahuah (God) truly, and shall bury their idols.* The collection for Jerusalem is the turning made tangible, carnal things paid back for spiritual things received (Romans 15:27).
writer_flag: The old note equated Paul's Gentiles with the nations themselves. Rewritten so Paul's Gentiles are the scattered seed living as Gentiles (the skill's reading), with Tobit's turning of the nations kept as what he saw. Please check that framing. Also removed 'substance' from the prose.

apoc_text: For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.
old_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *A pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty* — the older book describes what flows out from the glory without diminishing it, and Hebrews fastens that same picture to a person: *the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person* (Hebrews 1:3). The Son proceeds from the Father as brightness proceeds from light, the same in substance, distinct in standing — Elohim who has a Father, the Formed who shines out the Formless.
new_note: *For she is the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). *Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;* (Hebrews 1:3). A pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: Wisdom describes something that comes out of the glory without lessening it. Hebrews puts a person where Wisdom put a picture. The Son is the brightness of his glory and the express image of his person, the way light shining is of the light and yet is not the lamp. He proceeds from the Father as brightness proceeds from light, the Formed shining out from the Formless: Elohim (God) who has a Father, the one who upholds all things by the word of his power and then sat down at the right hand of the one he came from.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 — *a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.* What flows out from the glory without lessening it is a person in Hebrews 1:3, the brightness of his glory.

apoc_text: Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.
old_note: Ecclesiasticus 23:19 — *Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.* Ben Sira's brighter-than-the-sun eyes are the same all-hearing ear of jealousy from which murmuring is not hid in Wisdom 1:10.
new_note: *Such a man only fears the eyes of men, and knoweth not that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men, and considering the most secret parts.* (Ecclesiasticus 23:19). *For the ear of jealousy heareth all things: and the noise of murmurings is not hid.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:10). Sirach describes the man who fears only the eyes of men and forgets that the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, searching out the most secret places. The Wisdom of Solomon says the same of his hearing — the ear of jealousy hears everything, and murmuring is not hidden. Nothing done in the dark and nothing muttered under the breath escapes him. The two books together close every hiding place: he sees what the walls cover and hears what the voice keeps low.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 23:19 — *the eyes of Yahuah (God) are ten thousand times brighter than the sun.* The eyes that see the secret parts and the ear that hears all murmuring (Wisdom of Solomon 1:10).

apoc_text: For your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.
old_note: John 6:33 — *For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* The sweetness of the heavenly sustenance in Wisdom of Solomon 16:21 finds its substance in the Bread that gives life to the world.
new_note: *For your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children, and serving to the appetite of the eater, tempered itself to every man’s liking.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:21). *For the bread of Elohim (God) is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.* (John 6:33). The manna carried the Father's sweetness to his children and fitted itself to every one who ate it. John names the bread of Elohim (God) as a person — he who comes down from heaven and gives life to the world. The sweetness the wilderness tasted was a foretaste of the one who came down; the manna fed a generation, and the Bread who came down gives life.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:21 — *your sustenance declared your sweetness to your children.* The sweetness the wilderness tasted is the Bread who comes down and gives life to the world (John 6:33).

apoc_text: And brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.
old_note: Hebrews 4:12 — *For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.* The Word-as-sharp-sword of Wisdom 18:16, now turned inward to discern the heart.
new_note: *And brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:16). *For the word of Elohim (God) is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.* (Hebrews 4:12). In Egypt the word came as a sharp sword that filled the land with death, touching heaven and standing on the earth. Hebrews says the same word is still a sword, sharper than any two-edged blade, and it now cuts where no Egyptian saw it fall — between soul and spirit, into the thoughts and intents of the heart. The sword is the same; the field it works has moved inward. The one who judged Egypt in a night reads the heart of the one who reads him.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 18:16 — *brought your unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword.* The same sword, now sharper than any twoedged sword and turned on the heart (Hebrews 4:12).

apoc_text: Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.
old_note: Matthew 23:28 — *Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.* The Messiah indicts exactly the hypocrite-in-the-sight-of-men of Sir 1:29.
new_note: *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:29). *Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.* (Matthew 23:28). Sirach gives the counsel; Yahusha (Jesus) delivers the indictment of the men who ignored it. To be a hypocrite in the sight of men is to appear righteous unto men while being something else within, which is exactly how Matthew 23:28 reads. The warning came first, in a book the Reformation later cut from the library, and the Messiah's woe assumes his hearers should have known better. The religious system of his day had built itself on appearance; Sirach had told Yashar'el (Israel) long before that appearance is not what Yahuah (God) is weighing.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 1:29 — *Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heed what you speak.* The Messiah's woe at Matthew 23:28 indicts exactly this man.

apoc_text: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.
old_note: Ecclesiastes 12:13 — *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.* The fear-plus-keep-the-commandments of Sir 1:26 is the whole duty of man.
new_note: *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments, and Yahuah (God) shall give her to you.* (Ecclesiasticus 1:26). *Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear Elohim (God), and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.* (Ecclesiastes 12:13). Sirach puts wisdom on the far side of the commandments: keep them, and Yahuah (God) gives her. Solomon ends his whole book in the same place, fear Elohim (God) and keep his commandments, and calls that the whole duty of man. Neither writer knows a wisdom that stands apart from the commandments or a fear of Yahuah (God) that outgrows them. The commandments are not the beginner's course a wise man leaves behind; they are the door wisdom comes through, and the conclusion the wisest man in Yashar'el (Israel) arrived at.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 1:26 — *If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments.* Solomon's conclusion of the whole matter, in one line (Ecclesiastes 12:13).

apoc_text: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
old_note: 1 Peter 1:7 — *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):* Peter's gold-tried-with-fire is ben Sira's furnace of adversity verbatim in figure (Sirach 2:5).
new_note: *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). *That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):* (1 Peter 1:7). Peter writes to the scattered strangers with Sirach's figure in his hand: faith tried with fire, more precious than gold that perishes. Sirach had said gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity, and Peter, who had been through that furnace himself the night the cock crowed, hands the picture on to the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) he is writing to. The trial is not a sign of being forsaken; it is the proving, and what is proved is found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ). The Apocrypha and the apostle are describing the same furnace.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 2:5 — *gold is tried in the fire.* Peter's faith tried with fire at 1 Peter 1:7 is Sirach's figure handed on.

apoc_text: As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.
old_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:6 — *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.* The companion wisdom book self-links the very gold-in-the-furnace proving of the righteous that Sirach 2:5 declares.
new_note: *As gold in the furnace has he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:6). *For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.* (Ecclesiasticus 2:5). Two wisdom books, one furnace. Sirach says gold is tried in the fire and acceptable men in the furnace of adversity; Wisdom says Yahuah (God) tried the righteous as gold in the furnace and received them as a burnt offering. The fire does not destroy the gold; it shows what the gold is. The righteous who were tormented and killed in Wisdom 2 were being refined, not discarded, and what came through the fire was received at the altar.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:6 — *As gold in the furnace has he tried them.* Sirach says the same at Ecclesiasticus 2:5 — *acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.*

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The sister apocryphal wisdom-book teaches the same: alms quench sin as water quencheth fire (Ecclesiasticus 3:30).
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *Water will quench a flaming fire; and alms makes an atonement for sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:30). Two books of the library say one thing in two pictures. Tobit's open hand keeps the face of Yahuah (God) turned toward the giver; Sirach says alms put out sin the way water puts out fire. Neither is buying anything. Alms is mercy, mercy is what the Torah asks of a man, and the one who walks in it walks in the light of the Father's face.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* Sirach's picture of the same mercy: *alms makes an atonement for sins* as water quenches fire (Ecclesiasticus 3:30).

apoc_text: Strive for the truth to death, and Yahuah (God) shall fight for you.
old_note: Matthew 10:32 — *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* To strive for the truth to death (Sirach 4:28) with Yahuah fighting for thee is the confessing-unto-the-end the Messiah crowns before the Father.
new_note: *Strive for the truth to death, and Yahuah (God) shall fight for you.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:28). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Sirach tells his son to strive for the truth to death, and promises that Yahuah (God) will do the fighting. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve that whoever confesses him before men will be confessed before the Father. Confessing him before men is the striving for the truth, carried all the way to death if it comes to that, and the confession before the Father is Yahuah (God) fighting for the one who did not let go. The promise in Sirach and the promise in Matthew are the same promise: the man who holds the truth in front of men is not left to hold it alone.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:28 — *Strive for the truth to death, and Yahuah (God) shall fight for you.* The confession before men that is confessed before the Father (Matthew 10:32).

apoc_text: He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless.
old_note: Proverbs 8:21 — *That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.* Wisdom's inheritance for those who love her is the glory Sirach 4:13 says he that holdeth her fast shall inherit.
new_note: *He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory; and wherever she entereth, Yahuah (God) will bless.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:13). *That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance; and I will fill their treasures.* (Proverbs 8:21). Wisdom speaks for herself in Proverbs: she causes those who love her to inherit, and she fills their treasures. Sirach describes the same inheritance from the receiving end: the one who holds her fast inherits glory, and wherever she enters, Yahuah (God) blesses. Both verses give wisdom an estate to leave, and both leave it to the ones who love her and will not let her go. Holding her fast is the inheritance's condition and its proof.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:13 — *He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory.* Wisdom's inheritance for those who love her, Proverbs 8:21.
writer_flag: Proverbs 8:21 (canon text) contains the word 'substance' (*inherit substance*); it is scripture and left as it reads.

apoc_text: Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.
old_note: Proverbs 18:24 — *A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.* The proverb's "friend that sticketh closer than a brother" is the rare one-of-a-thousand counsellor Ben Sira tells you to seek in Sirach 6:6.
new_note: *Be in peace with many: nevertheless have but one counsellor of a thousand.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:6). *A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.* (Proverbs 18:24). Solomon's proverb has two kinds of friend in it: the many a friendly man gathers, and the one who sticks closer than a brother. Sirach draws the same line and tells you how to count: be at peace with many, but take one counsellor out of a thousand. The crowd of friends is not the problem; letting the crowd counsel you is. Both writers are pointing at the rare one, the friend whose word you can build on, and both say you will not find him by being friendly to everyone but by proving him.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 6:6 — *have but one counsellor of a thousand.* The friend that sticketh closer than a brother of Proverbs 18:24.

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you* — Tobit's almsgiving charge, the apocryphal sibling to Sirach 7:32's hand stretched to the poor.
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32). Tobit tells his son to turn his face toward the poor; Sirach tells his to stretch out his hand to them so that his blessing may be perfected. The face and the hand together are the whole posture of the righteous man in the library: see the need and move toward it. The blessing is not finished until the hand is open.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *neither turn your face from any poor.* Sirach adds the hand to the face: *stretch yours hand to the poor, that your blessing may be perfected* (Ecclesiasticus 7:32).
writer_flag: Live-text misprint in Ecclesiasticus 7:32: 'stretch yours hand' (should be 'your hand'). Quoted as it stands.

apoc_text: Fear Yahuah (God), and honor the priest; and give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.
old_note: Proverbs 3:9 — *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase* — the firstfruits-portion Sirach 7:31 names among the priest's due.
new_note: *Fear Yahuah (God), and honor the priest; and give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits, and the trespass offering, and the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the firstfruits of the holy things.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:31). *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:* (Proverbs 3:9). Sirach puts the priest's portion under the fear of Yahuah (God) and says it is given as it is commanded — the firstfruits, the trespass offering, the shoulder, the holy things. Solomon had already said where that honor is going: the firstfruits of all the increase honor Yahuah (LORD) himself, and the priest is the hand that receives them for him. Neither verse treats the gift as a tax. It is the first and the best handed back to the one who gave the whole, and the Torah's instruction for the priest's due is where that honor lands in practice.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:31 — *give him his portion, as it is commanded you; the firstfruits.* The firstfruits that honor Yahuah (LORD) in Proverbs 3:9 reach him through the priest's hand.

apoc_text: As near as you can, guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.
old_note: Proverbs 13:20 — *He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.* the consult-with-the-wise counsel of Sirach 9:14-15.
new_note: *As near as you can, guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:14). *He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.* (Proverbs 13:20). Sirach says to take the measure of your neighbour as best you can and to take counsel from the wise, and in the next verse he says to let all your communication be in the law of the Most High. Solomon had said the same about company: walk with the wise and you grow wise, keep company with fools and you share their ruin. Who sits at your table shapes who you become.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 9:14 — *guess at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.* Sirach's consult with the wise is Solomon's walk with wise men at Proverbs 13:20.

apoc_text: Let your talk be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the Most High.
old_note: Psalm 1:2 — *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night.* the law-of-the-Most-High talk Sirach 9:15 says fills the wise man's communication.
new_note: *Let your talk be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the Most High.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:15). *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night.* (Psalm 1:2). Sirach puts the whole of the wise man's conversation inside the law of the Most High. David's blessed man delights in the law of Yahuah (LORD) and meditates in it day and night. The one who delights in it will talk about it; the man whose speech is in the Torah is the man whose heart has been there first.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 9:15 — *all your communication in the law of the Most High.* Talk in the law of the Most High is the delight in the law of Psalm 1:2 spoken aloud.

apoc_text: Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.
old_note: Matthew 5:28 — *But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* the Messiah taking Sirach 9:8's turn-away-the-eye to the heart's root.
new_note: *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman, and look not upon another’s beauty; for many have been deceived by the beauty of a woman; for herewith love is kindled as a fire.* (Ecclesiasticus 9:8). *But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* (Matthew 5:28). Sirach tells the eye to turn away before love is kindled as a fire, because the deception begins in the looking. Yahusha (Jesus) follows the same line to its root: the look that lusts has already committed the adultery in the heart. Neither is adding a new commandment to the seventh. Both are reading it where it was always meant to be read, at the eye and the heart, before the body ever moves.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 9:8 — *Turn away your eye from a beautiful woman.* The eye turned away in Sirach is the heart Yahusha (Jesus) reads at Matthew 5:28.

apoc_text: My son, according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.
old_note: Job 1:21 — *And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) hath taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Job's surrender frames the do-good-to-thyself-and-give-Yahuah-his-due of Sirach 14:11.
new_note: *My son, according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.* (Ecclesiasticus 14:11). *And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: Yahuah (LORD) gave, and Yahuah (LORD) hath taken away; blessed be the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Job 1:21). Sirach says to do good to yourself as you are able and to give Yahuah (God) his due offering, and his very next line is the reason: death will not be long in coming. Job said at the ash heap what Sirach is building on — a man comes naked and goes back naked, and what he had in between was Yahuah's (God's) to give and to take. Everything in the hand is on loan. Give the Giver his due while it is still in your hand to give.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 14:11 — *according to your ability do good to thyself, and give Yahuah (God) his due offering.* Give Yahuah (God) his due while it is in your hand; Job 1:21 says who gave it and who takes it.

apoc_text: For the wisdom of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things:
old_note: Proverbs 15:3 — *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.* Sirach's all-beholding Yahuah (Sirach 15:18) is the proverb's eyes-in-every-place.
new_note: *For the wisdom of Yahuah (God) is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things:* (Ecclesiasticus 15:18). *The eyes of Yahuah (LORD) are in every place, beholding the evil and the good.* (Proverbs 15:3). Sirach says the wisdom of Yahuah (God) beholds all things and his power is great. Solomon put the same truth in one line: his eyes are in every place, on the evil and the good alike. The verses before this in Sirach say life and death are set before a man and he will be given what he chooses; the all-seeing eye is why the choice is weighed and not forgotten.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 15:18 — *he is mighty in power, and beholds all things.* Sirach's all-beholding Yahuah (God) is the eyes in every place of Proverbs 15:3.

apoc_text: For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.
old_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* Ben Sira's own diagnosis self-linking pride=the-beginning-of-sin to the proud abhorred in Sirach 16:8.
new_note: *For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it shall pour out abomination: and therefore Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* (Ecclesiasticus 10:13). *Neither spared he the place where Lot sojourned, but abhorred them for their pride.* (Ecclesiasticus 16:8). Sirach's own proof case for pride comes later in his book: the place where Lot sojourned was not spared, and the reason he gives is their pride. The verse here says pride pours out abomination and brings strange calamities; the later verse names the city it happened to. Sodom is not a story about one sin. It is where pride ends when it is left to pour.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 10:13 — *Yahuah (God) brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.* The strange calamities of pride land on the place where Lot sojourned at Ecclesiasticus 16:8.

apoc_text: Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.
old_note: Ezekiel 18:30 — *Therefore I will judge you, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), every one according to his ways, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD). Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.* Sirach 17:26 'turn away from iniquity' is Ezekiel's turn-and-be-saved call.
new_note: *Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity: for he will lead you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:26). *Therefore I will judge you, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), every one according to his ways, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD). Repent, and turn yourselves from all your transgressions; so iniquity shall not be your ruin.* (Ezekiel 18:30). Sirach says to turn again to the Most High and away from iniquity, and promises light at the end of it. Ezekiel says the same to the house of Yashar'el (Israel): repent, turn from your transgressions, so iniquity shall not be your ruin. The turn is what keeps iniquity from being the end of the story. Judgment according to a man's ways and the open call to turn stand in the same verse because they are the same mercy.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:26 — *Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from iniquity.* Turn away from iniquity is Ezekiel's so iniquity shall not be your ruin at Ezekiel 18:30.

apoc_text: But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.
old_note: Ezekiel 18:32 — *For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD): wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.* The mercy granting return in Sirach 17:24 is Yahuah's no-pleasure-in-death heart.
new_note: *But to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:24). *For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD): wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.* (Ezekiel 18:32). Sirach says return is granted to them that repent. Ezekiel heard the heart behind it: Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) has no pleasure in the death of the one who dies, and so he calls, turn yourselves, and live. The granting of return is not reluctant. It is what he wanted all along.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:24 — *to them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.* Return granted to the penitent is the no pleasure in the death of him that dieth of Ezekiel 18:32.

apoc_text: Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less.
old_note: James 4:8 — *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.* 'Make your prayer before his face, and offend less' (Sirach 17:25) is James' draw-nigh-and-cleanse summons.
new_note: *Return to Yahuah (God), and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend less.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:25). *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.* (James 4:8). Sirach says to return, forsake sins, pray before his face, and offend less. James says to draw nigh to Elohim (God) and he will draw nigh to you, and he says it to sinners with unclean hands and double minds. Both put the turning first and the nearness after. The prayer before his face and the drawing nigh are one movement, and both expect the hands to be cleansed on the way.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 17:25 — *make your prayer before his face, and offend less.* Prayer before his face and offending less is James's draw nigh and cleanse your hands at James 4:8.

apoc_text: Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.
old_note: Galatians 5:16 — *This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.* Sha'ul's Spirit-walk is Sirach 18:30's refrain-thyself-from-thy-appetites.
new_note: *Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:30). *This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.* (Galatians 5:16). Sirach tells his son to refrain himself from his appetites rather than follow his lusts. Paul tells the Galatians how that refraining is done: walk in the Spirit, and the lust of the flesh will not be fulfilled. The Spirit does not loosen the standard Sirach set; he supplies the strength to keep it. Walking in the Spirit is the way a man refrains himself, and the commandments are where that walk goes.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:30 — *Go not after your lusts, but refrain thyself from your appetites.* The refraining Sirach commands is done by walking in the Spirit (Galatians 5:16).

apoc_text: Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.
old_note: James 1:19 — *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.* Ya'akov's swift-to-hear is Sirach 18:19's learn-before-you-speak in the same wisdom stream.
new_note: *Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:19). *Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:* (James 1:19). Sirach puts learning before speaking the way a wise man takes his medicine before the sickness comes — the order matters. James says the same in three strokes: swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. Both put the ear ahead of the mouth, and both treat it as wisdom you practice before the moment arrives, not after.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:19 — *Learn before you speak, and use physick or ever you be sick.* Learning before speaking is James' *swift to hear, slow to speak* (James 1:19).

apoc_text: Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.
old_note: Ecclesiastes 5:4 — *When thou vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.* Qoheleth's defer-not-thy-vow is the very law Sirach 18:22 echoes — pay in due time, defer not till death.
new_note: *Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time, and defer not until death to be justified.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:22). *When thou vowest a vow unto Elohim (God), defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.* (Ecclesiastes 5:4). Solomon wrote the rule: a vow made to Elohim (God) is to be paid without delay, because he has no pleasure in fools. Sirach is holding that rule when he tells his son to let nothing hinder the paying of a vow in due time, and he presses it one step further — do not put off until death the matter of being justified before Yahuah (God). The vow deferred and the turning deferred are the same folly.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:22 — *Let nothing hinder you to pay your vow in due time.* The rule of Ecclesiastes 5:4, *defer not to pay it*, carried into Sirach's counsel.

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The same restored-library wisdom: give without the envious eye that blemishes the deed in Sirach 18:15.
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use uncomfortable words when you give any thing.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:15). Tobit warns against the envious eye when giving; Sirach warns against the sour word. Both know that a gift can be spoiled by the spirit it comes in. The alms Yahuah (God) looks on is given gladly, without a grudging eye and without a hard word to the one who receives it.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *when you give alms, let not your eye be envious.* Sirach's twin warning, not to blemish the good deed with uncomfortable words (Ecclesiasticus 18:15).

apoc_text: The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.
old_note: Psalm 145:9 — *Yahuah (LORD) is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.* This is the mercy-upon-all-flesh of Sirach 18:13 word for word — tender mercies over all His works.
new_note: *The mercy of man is toward his neighbour; but the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh: he reproveth, and nurtureth, and teaches and brings again, as a shepherd his flock.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:13). *Yahuah (LORD) is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.* (Psalm 145:9). David sang it first: Yahuah (LORD) is good to all, and his tender mercies rest over everything he has made. Sirach sets the same truth beside the mercy of a man, which reaches only his neighbour, and shows how much wider the mercy of Yahuah (God) runs — over all flesh, as a shepherd over the whole flock. The psalm and the wisdom book are saying one thing in two voices.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:13 — *the mercy of Yahuah (God) is upon all flesh.* The tender mercies over all his works in Psalm 145:9, said again.

apoc_text: The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.
old_note: Psalm 103:15 — *As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.* The hundred-year span of Sirach 18:9 is the same flower-of-the-field brevity the Psalmist sings.
new_note: *The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.* (Ecclesiasticus 18:9). *As for man, his days are as grass: as a flower of the field, so he flourisheth.* (Psalm 103:15). Sirach puts the limit on a man's days at a hundred years at the most, and in the next verse calls a thousand years a drop of water to the sea beside eternity. David says man's days are as grass and he flourishes as a flower of the field. A hundred years and a flower's season are the same length against eternity, and both writers say it so the reader will spend them rightly.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 18:9 — *The number of a man’s days at the most are an hundred years.* A hundred years at the most is the flower of the field of Psalm 103:15.

apoc_text: A man may be known by his look, and one that has understanding by his countenance, when you meetest him.
old_note: Matthew 7:16 — *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?* Sira's 'a man may be known by his look' is Yeshua's know-them-by-fruits: the inward deceit shows itself outwardly.
new_note: *A man may be known by his look, and one that has understanding by his countenance, when you meetest him.* (Ecclesiasticus 19:29). *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?* (Matthew 7:16). Sirach says a man can be known by his look, and a man of understanding by his countenance, before he has said a word. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the surer test: you will know them by their fruits, because thorns do not yield grapes. Both say the same thing about the inward man — what is in him comes out where it can be seen, whether in the face or in the fruit.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 19:29 — *A man may be known by his look.* What is inward shows outwardly; *Ye shall know them by their fruits* (Matthew 7:16).

apoc_text: There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.
old_note: Proverbs 17:28 — *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.* The same paradox Ben Sira sets down in Sirach 20:5 — silence itself confers the appearance, and the substance, of wisdom.
new_note: *There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise: and another by much babbling becometh hateful.* (Ecclesiasticus 20:5). *Even a fool, when he holdeth his peace, is counted wise: and he that shutteth his lips is esteemed a man of understanding.* (Proverbs 17:28). Solomon noticed that even a fool who holds his peace is counted wise. Sirach says it from the other side: one man keeps silence and is found wise, another babbles and makes himself hateful. Both are telling the same thing — the mouth gives a man away, and the one who can shut it is already halfway to understanding.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 20:5 — *There is one that keepeth silence, and is found wise.* The same paradox as Proverbs 17:28 — the fool who holds his peace is counted wise.

apoc_text: He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.
old_note: Proverbs 9:10 — *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* The fear-of-Yahuah-is-wisdom refrain Ben Sira makes the crown of law-keeping (Ecclesiasticus 21:11).
new_note: *He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof: and the perfection of the fear of Yahuah (God) is wisdom.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:11). *The fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.* (Proverbs 9:10). Solomon set the foundation: the fear of Yahuah (LORD) is the beginning of wisdom. Sirach shows where it goes — the one who keeps the law of Yahuah (God) gets understanding of it, and the fear of Yahuah (God) brought to its perfection is wisdom itself. Fear is the beginning, keeping the law is the road, and wisdom is the crown of it. Understanding comes to the one who keeps, not to the one who only studies.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 21:11 — *He that keepeth the law of Yahuah (God) getteth the understanding thereof.* The fear of Yahuah (LORD) that begins wisdom in Proverbs 9:10 is made perfect in keeping the law.

apoc_text: My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.
old_note: Proverbs 9:6 — *Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.* The turn-and-sin-no-more wisdom of Ben Sira's opening call (Ecclesiasticus 21:1).
new_note: *My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* (Ecclesiasticus 21:1). *Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding.* (Proverbs 9:6). Wisdom's call in Proverbs is to forsake the foolish and live, and to walk in the way of understanding. Sirach opens his chapter with the same turn, put as a father puts it to a son — if you have sinned, do so no more, and ask pardon. Forsaking and turning are one motion; the way of understanding begins where the former sins are left behind.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 21:1 — *do so no more, but ask pardon for your former sins.* The turn Wisdom calls for in Proverbs 9:6 — forsake the foolish, and live.

apoc_text: He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?
old_note: Matthew 18:21 — *Then came Peter to him, and said, Yahuah (Lord), how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?* Peter's question opens the very mercy-toward-an-equal that Sirach 28:4 demands of him *which is like himself*.
new_note: *He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?* (Ecclesiasticus 28:4). *Then came Peter to him, and said, Adonai (Lord), how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?* (Matthew 18:21). Peter's question is about a brother, a man like himself, sinning against him over and over. Sirach had already asked what becomes of a man who shows no mercy to one made like himself and then asks forgiveness for his own sins. Peter is standing right at that question, counting toward a limit, and the King's answer in the next verse takes the limit away. The mercy owed to an equal is the mercy Sirach demands, and it is the mercy a disciple must give before he asks his own.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 28:4 — *He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself.* Peter's *how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him?* (Matthew 18:21) stands right at Sirach's question about mercy to the man like yourself.

apoc_text: Lend to your neighbour in time of his need, and pay you your neighbour again in due season.
old_note: Matthew 5:42 — *Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.* The Messiah's Sermon-on-the-Mount word is Sirach 29:2 made fuller: lend to your neighbour in his need.
new_note: *Lend to your neighbour in time of his need, and pay you your neighbour again in due season.* (Ecclesiasticus 29:2). *Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.* (Matthew 5:42). Sirach says lend to your neighbour when he needs it, and pay back your neighbour when the time comes. Yahusha (Jesus) on the mount says give to him who asks, and do not turn away the one who wants to borrow. The Sermon takes Sirach's line and opens the hand wider, but it is the same hand. Lending to a neighbour in his need was already the commandment in Yashar'el (Israel); the King was telling his disciples to keep it without flinching.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 29:2 — *Lend to your neighbour in time of his need.* The open hand of Matthew 5:42, *from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away*, is Sirach's lending to the neighbour in his need.

apoc_text: If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it.
old_note: Proverbs 23:2 — *And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.* Solomon's knife-to-the-throat at the ruler's table is Ben Sira's be not greedy at the bountiful table in Sirach 31:12.
new_note: *If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it, and say not, There is much meat on it.* (Ecclesiasticus 31:12). *And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.* (Proverbs 23:2). Solomon tells the man given to appetite to put a knife to his own throat when he sits at a ruler's table; Sirach tells him not to be greedy at a bountiful table or to say, There is much meat here. It is the same instruction in two voices, generations apart. A full table is a test of the eye and the hand, and both wisdom writers lay the restraint on the guest, not on the host.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 31:12 — *If you sit at a bountiful table, be not greedy upon it.* Solomon's knife to the throat (Proverbs 23:2) is the same restraint at the same table.

apoc_text: Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor doeth as one that killeth the son before his father’s eyes.
old_note: Proverbs 28:8 — *He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.* the offering from *the goods of the poor* in Sirach 34:20 is Proverbs' unjust gain that only stores up for the merciful.
new_note: *Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor doeth as one that killeth the son before his father’s eyes.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:20). *He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor.* (Proverbs 28:8). Sirach says the man who brings an offering out of the goods of the poor is like one who kills a son in front of his father. Solomon says the man who grows rich by usury and unjust gain is only gathering it up for someone who will pity the poor. Both are talking about the same money. Taken from the poor and carried to the altar it is an abomination; held by the one who took it, it will not stay, for by the hand of Yahuah (God) it ends up with the merciful, and the one who gathered it is left with nothing but the blood on his hands.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 34:20 — *Whoso brings an offering of the goods of the poor.* Unjust gain only gathers for the merciful (Proverbs 28:8); offered at the altar it is bloodshed.

apoc_text: Great travail is created for every man, and an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, till the day that they return to the mother of all things.
old_note: Job 14:1 — *Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.* Job states the same travail-from-the-womb that Sirach 40:1 lays on every son of Adam.
new_note: *Great travail is created for every man, and an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, till the day that they return to the mother of all things.* (Ecclesiasticus 40:1). *Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.* (Job 14:1). Job and Sirach are looking at the same life. Job says the man born of a woman has few days and all of them full of trouble; Sirach says the heavy yoke lies on the sons of Adam from the day they leave the womb until the day they go back into the earth that is the mother of all things. Neither one is complaining about bad luck. They are describing the sentence laid on Adam in the garden, sorrow all his days and a return to the dust (Genesis 3:17–19), carried down the line to every son born of him.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 40:1 — *an heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam, from the day that they go out of their mother’s womb.* Job 14:1 says the same of the man born of a woman: few days, full of trouble, the yoke laid on Adam carried down his line.

apoc_text: Who kept the law of the Most High, and was in covenant with him: he established the covenant in his flesh; and when he was proved, he was found faithful.
old_note: Genesis 17:1 — *And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.* The walk-before-me-and-be-perfect of this covenant chapter is the law of the Most High Abraham kept in Sirach 44:20.
new_note: *Who kept the law of the Most High, and was in covenant with him: he established the covenant in his flesh; and when he was proved, he was found faithful.* (Ecclesiasticus 44:20). *And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be thou perfect.* (Genesis 17:1). Sirach says Abraham kept the law of the Most High, and he says it of a man who lived centuries before Sinai. Genesis 17 shows what that law was: Yahuah (God) appears and commands him to walk before him and be perfect, and in the same chapter gives him the covenant in his flesh, the circumcision Sirach names (Genesis 17:10–11). When Yahuah (God) later speaks of Abraham he says he *obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws* (Genesis 26:5). The commandments did not begin with Moses; Abraham walked in them, and when he was proved on the mountain he was found faithful.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 44:20 — *Who kept the law of the Most High, and was in covenant with him.* The law Abraham kept is the walk Yahuah (God) commanded at Genesis 17:1, and the covenant in his flesh is the circumcision of the same chapter.

apoc_text: Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came.
old_note: Hebrews 11:7 — *By faith Noah, being warned of Elohim (God) of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.* Hebrews makes Noah's exchange-for-the-world (Sirach 44:17) an act of saving faith.
new_note: *Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came.* (Ecclesiasticus 44:17). *By faith Noah, being warned of Elohim (God) of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith.* (Hebrews 11:7). Sirach says Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant to the earth when the flood came; Hebrews says Noah believed a warning about things not yet seen and built an ark, condemning the world by doing it. These are not two different Noahs. The righteousness Genesis saw in him, *Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with Elohim (God)* (Genesis 6:9), was faith with its hands on the timber. He is the first remnant in scripture, one household kept alive through the wrath while the world around it perished, and Sirach calls the trade by its name: he was taken in exchange for the world.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 44:17 — *Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world.* Hebrews 11:7 shows the faith behind the righteousness: Noah believed what was not yet seen and built, and was left as a remnant.

apoc_text: All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.
old_note: Hebrews 11:1 — *Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.* The faith Hebrews defines is the very glory by which the fathers of Sirach 44:7 were honoured in their generations.
new_note: *All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.* (Ecclesiasticus 44:7). *Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.* (Hebrews 11:1). Sirach's roll of honoured men and the roll of Hebrews 11 are the same men: Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, the prophets. Sirach says they were the glory of their times; Hebrews says what made them so, they held things hoped for as already theirs and lived on the evidence of what they had not yet seen. Hebrews finishes the roll by saying they all died without receiving the promise, waiting for us so that they would not be made perfect without us (Hebrews 11:39–40). The glory of their generations was a faith that is still waiting for the resurrection to be paid out.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 44:7 — *All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.* The honoured men of Sirach 44 are the roll of Hebrews 11; the glory of their times was faith in things not yet seen.
writer_flag: Live Hebrews 11:1 text contains the word 'substance' inside the quoted verse itself; left as scripture reads.

apoc_text: He stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour to the most high King of all.
old_note: Hebrews 9:12 — *Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.* The poured-out cup of Simon's offering (Sirach 50:15) is the shadow whose substance is the Messiah entering once with His own blood — the type, not the fulfilment.
new_note: *He stretched out his hand to the cup, and poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour to the most high King of all.* (Ecclesiasticus 50:15). *Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.* (Hebrews 9:12). Simon the high priest finishes the altar service by pouring the blood of the grape at the foot of the altar, a sweet savour to the most high King. Yahusha (Jesus) took that same cup of the vine on his last night and said *this is my blood of the new testament* (Matthew 26:28). Hebrews says he then entered the holy place once, not with the blood of goats and calves but with his own. The wine poured at the altar's foot was showing in the fruit of the grape what the Messiah (Christ) would do in his own blood; Simon poured the picture, and the high priest after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) poured out the thing itself.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 50:15 — *poured of the blood of the grape, he poured out at the foot of the altar a sweetsmelling savour.* The blood of the grape at the altar's foot pictures what Hebrews 9:12 says the Messiah (Christ) did with his own blood, once.

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The charity-tithe given 'to them to whom it was meet' in Tobit 1:8 is the same alms-righteousness Tobit later commands his son.
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *And the third I gave to them to whom it was meet, as Debora my father’s mother had commanded me, because I was left an orphan by my father.* (Tobit 1:8). Tobit 1:8 shows the old man doing as a young man what he later teaches: the third tithe given to those to whom it was meet, as his grandmother Debora had commanded him. Three generations carry it, Debora to Tobit, Tobit to Tobias. The alms he charges on his son in chapter 4 is a tithe he had been paying since he was an orphan.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The charge to his son is the third tithe Tobit himself paid from his orphan years (Tobit 1:8).

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: Tobit 4:7 — *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The alms his wife throws in his face are the very practice Tobit will charge upon his son as the way of righteousness.
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *But she replied upon me, It was given for a gift more than the wages. Howbeit I did not believe her, but told her render it to the owners: and I was abashed at her. But she replied upon me, Where are your alms and your righteous deeds? behold, you and all your works are known.* (Tobit 2:14). Blind and poor, Tobit is mocked by his own wife: where are your alms and your righteous deeds now? He does not take the words back. Two chapters later he hands the same practice to his son as the way to keep the face of Yahuah (God) toward him. The reproach did not move him, because alms were never a trade for comfort; they were covenant life, kept in blindness as in sight.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* The alms Anna threw in his face are the alms he charges on his son (Tobit 2:14).

apoc_text: Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.
old_note: Luke 11:41 — *But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.* Yahusha makes almsgiving the inward cleansing — exactly Tobit's 'give of thy substance' that keeps Yahuah's face turned toward the giver.
new_note: *Give alms of your substance; and when you give alms, let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor, and the face of Yahuah (God) shall not be turned away from you.* (Tobit 4:7). *But rather give alms of such things as ye have; and, behold, all things are clean unto you.* (Luke 11:41). The Pharisees were careful about the outside of the cup; Yahusha (Jesus) told them the cleansing they needed was to give alms of what they had. Tobit had told his son the same long before: give of what you have, turn your face from no poor man, and the face of Yahuah (God) stays toward you. The King is not inventing a new rule; he is pointing a religious system back to the mercy the library had been teaching every son.
member_note: Tobit 4:7 — *let not your eye be envious, neither turn your face from any poor.* The alms that make all things clean (Luke 11:41) are the alms Tobit charged on his son.

apoc_text: And now, O Yahuah (God), I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.
old_note: Malachi 2:15 — *And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.* The godly-seed purpose of marriage is precisely Tobias’s not-for-lust-but-uprightly (Tobit 8:7).
new_note: *And now, O Yahuah (God), I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly: therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.* (Tobit 8:7). *And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.* (Malachi 2:15). Tobias tells Yahuah (God) why he is taking Sarah: not for lust but uprightly, that they may grow old together. Malachi asks why Yahuah (God) made the two one and answers it — that he might seek a godly seed — and warns the man not to deal treacherously with the wife of his youth. Tobias's prayer is that purpose spoken aloud at the start of a marriage. The seed of promise is carried through marriages entered this way, and the prophet and the young bridegroom agree on what marriage is for.
member_note: Tobit 8:7 — *I take not this my sister for lust but uprightly.* Marriage entered uprightly, for the godly seed Malachi says it was made for (Malachi 2:15).

apoc_text: Charging them to keep the passages of the hill country: for by them there was an entrance into Judea, and it was easy to stop them that would come up, because the passage was straight, for two men at the most.
old_note: Daniel 11:30 — *For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant.* the same tyrant-against-the-covenant pattern Judith 4:7 braces for at the passes into Judea.
new_note: *Charging them to keep the passages of the hill country: for by them there was an entrance into Judea, and it was easy to stop them that would come up, because the passage was straight, for two men at the most.* (Judith 4:7). *For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant.* (Daniel 11:30). Judith's Yashar'el (Israel) hears that the invader is coming and does two things: they hold the narrow passes into Judea, and they fast and cry to Yahuah (God) (Judith 4:9–13). Daniel describes the king such a people will keep facing, one whose indignation is against the holy covenant itself and who has intelligence with those inside who forsake it. The Maccabees would meet that king in Antiochus, and the pattern does not end there. The war is never only about the land; it is a war on the covenant, with help from the covenant's own deserters, and the people who keep it answer at the passes and on their knees.
member_note: Judith 4:7 — *it was easy to stop them that would come up, because the passage was straight.* The invader Judith's people brace for at the passes is the king of Daniel 11:30, whose indignation is against the holy covenant.

apoc_text: Let all creatures serve you: for you spakest, and they were made, you did send forth your spirit, and it created them, and there is none that can resist your voice.
old_note: Psalm 148:5 — *Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.* Judith 16:14 ('you spakest, and they were made') confesses the same creation-by-the-word for which Psalm 148 calls all creatures to praise.
new_note: *Let all creatures serve you: for you spakest, and they were made, you did send forth your spirit, and it created them, and there is none that can resist your voice.* (Judith 16:14). *Let them praise the name of Yahuah (LORD): for he commanded, and they were created.* (Psalm 148:5). Judith says the whole creation was made by speaking, you spoke and they were made, you sent forth your spirit and it created them. The psalm says the same of the heavens and the host of them: he commanded, and they were created, and that is why they are to praise his name. Moses wrote it as *Elohim (God) said, Let there be* with the Spirit moving on the waters (Genesis 1:2–3), and David wrote that *by the word of Yahuah (LORD) were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth* (Psalm 33:6). John names that Word: all things were made by him (John 1:3). What was made by a voice cannot resist that voice, and Judith says so.
member_note: Judith 16:14 — *for you spakest, and they were made, you did send forth your spirit, and it created them.* Creation by the spoken word; Psalm 148:5 calls all of it to praise the one who commanded, and they were created.

apoc_text: But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.
old_note: 1 Corinthians 1:27 — *But Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;* Yahuah disappointing a vast army by the hand of one widow (Judith 16:6) is the very weak-confound-the-mighty principle Paul preaches.
new_note: *But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.* (Judith 16:6). *But Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;* (1 Corinthians 1:27). The Almighty Yahuah (God) brought a whole army to nothing by the hand of one widow, and Judith's song says so without apology. Paul tells the Corinthians this is how Elohim (God) works on purpose: he chooses the weak things to confound the mighty and the foolish things to confound the wise, so that no flesh can glory in his presence (1 Corinthians 1:29). Holofernes bragged of what he would do to Yashar'el (Israel); the next verse of the song says the mighty one did not fall by young men or giants but by a woman. The hand of a woman is the weak thing, and the weak thing is what he chose.
member_note: Judith 16:6 — *the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.* Yahuah (God) bringing an army to nothing by the hand of a widow is the weak confounding the mighty of 1 Corinthians 1:27.

apoc_text: And now we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies,
old_note: Leviticus 26:41 — *And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:* The Torah foretold the giving-into-enemy-hands and the humbled heart that turns it back, the frame Esther prays inside.
new_note: *And now we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies,* (The Rest of Esther 14:6). *And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity:* (Leviticus 26:41). Esther's prayer follows the lines Moses laid down. Leviticus 26 said that if the people broke the covenant, Yahuah (God) himself would walk contrary to them and bring them into the land of their enemies, and that the way back would open when their uncircumcised hearts were humbled and they accepted the punishment as just. Esther does exactly that: we have sinned, you gave us into our enemies' hands, you are righteous. The enemy's hand is the covenant curse at work, not the covenant's end, and the next line in Leviticus is the promise, *then will I remember my covenant with Jacob* (Leviticus 26:42). Her humbled heart in Persia is the turn the Torah said would bring them home.
member_note: The Rest of Esther 14:6 — *we have sinned before you: therefore have you given us into the hands of our enemies.* Esther prays inside Leviticus 26:41, the sin named, the enemy's hand owned as just, the humbled heart that turns the curse toward home.

apoc_text: From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.
old_note: Deuteronomy 7:6 — *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* Israel taken 'from among all people' is Moses' chosen-above-all-people, the ground of Esther's confidence.
new_note: *From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.* (The Rest of Esther 14:5). *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* (Deuteronomy 7:6). Esther says she heard it in her youth, in the tribe of her family: Yahuah (God) took Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people for a perpetual inheritance.
